title: staged-rollout-contingency-simulator-notes-wip
summary: Working notes for a lightweight staged-rollout contingency simulator and decision matrix. Purpose: help product + SRE + serving runtime rehearse failure modes, decision thresholds, and communication steps before large LLM feature exposures. This doc is intentionally procedural and simulation-driven rather than theoretical.
objectives: 1) Define a compact set of contingency states (degrade, oscillation, cost-spike, behavioral-drift) and concrete signal thresholds for automated and manual gates. 2) Sketch a simulator scenario suite that can be reused by product, SRE, and solutions engineering to rehearse responses. 3) Provide a comms checklist and escalation flow that maps to those contingency states. 4) Surface telemetry gaps needed to reliably detect each state.
assumptions: - Feature launches are incremental: 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 100% exposure waves. - Models may be swapped (model variant fallback) or routed to cheaper quantized variants under load. - We rely on service-level streaming telemetry (per-request latency, per-token cost estimate, error-type counts, quality probes) and application-level metrics (user drop rate, NPS signal, rerank losses). - Canary windows run across multiple time zones and include synthetic probes and a small human review panel.
contingency_states: DEGRADE: sustained P99 latency > SLO threshold for > 5m OR error rate > 0.5% for 2m. OSCILLATION: repeated flip between low and high latency bands across backend variants within 10m (indicates routing thrash). COST_SPIKE: rolling 30m token-cost per request > 2x baseline for targeted cohort. BEHAVIORAL_DRIFT: automated eval suite score drop > 4% absolute on critical prompt set or increase in hallucination signals (safety heuristics) crossing guardrail. INFRA_SOFT_FAULT: node eviction events or instance reboots affecting >=10% of dedicated pool capacity.
stability_score_formula: StabilityScore = max(0, 100 - (weighted_latency_penalty + error_penalty + drift_penalty + cost_penalty + oscillation_penalty)). Weighting: latency_penalty = (P99_ms - target_ms)/10 clipped; error_penalty = 50 * error_rate; drift_penalty = 20 * eval_drop_pct; cost_penalty = 10 * (cost_multiplier - 1); oscillation_penalty = 30 if observed thrash else 0. This gives a single numeric heuristic used by the simulator to propose action levels (>=85: continue, 60-85: monitor closely/partial rollback, <60: rollback or traffic split).
simulator_scenarios:
- Scenario A: sudden 3x P99 due to kernel regression on a popular shard (simulate node-level CPU contention + KV cache misses). Goal: validate automated fallbacks and canary slice rollback within 6 minutes.
- Scenario B: cost anomaly from token-length shift (users send longer inputs) that inflates per-request token usage 2.8x. Goal: test autoscaling + rate-limit enforcement + automated notification templates.
- Scenario C: model-behavior regression across a multilingual slice detected by eval harness (eval_drop 6%). Goal: exercise human-review panel, staged rollback to previous model variant, and black-box logging capture for repro.
- Scenario D: oscillation caused by routing policy reacting to partial AZ degraded latency resulting in thrash between dedicated and hosted capacity. Goal: test circuit-breaker that pins routing for 15m when thrash detected.
- Scenario E: combined micro-failures (2% instance churn + 0.3% client error spike) producing noisy signals. Goal: verify detection thresholds and avoid false-positive rollbacks.
simulation_plan: 1) Run each scenario in the local rollout-sim harness with seeded RNG (config files under github/rollout-sim/configs/). 2) Inject telemetry stubs (latency distribution, token-cost histogram, eval-score time series). 3) Evaluate StabilityScore over time, log decision points, and produce a timeline. 4) For each decision, record operator step required: (a) auto-fallback executed, (b) suggested manual review, (c) rollback executed. 5) Produce a Post-Sim Playbook entry summarizing timings and any ambiguous conditions.
observability_requirements: - Per-route P50/P90/P99 latency and request count (1s granularity). - Per-token cost estimator and rolling 30m cost multiplier. - Automated eval harness job that runs critical prompt sets every 10m and emits score deltas. - Synthetic probes per cohort (canary and control) that exercise safety and hallucination checks. - Routing decision logs (why traffic moved between variants). - Circuit-breaker state machine events with timestamps. - Alerting: paged for StabilityScore < 50 or sustained P99 above double-SLO for 10m; slack-only for intermediate conditions.
runbook_snippets: - Immediate steps for "StabilityScore < 60 and P99 > 2x SLO": 1) Open incident in RG-ops with tag 'rollout'. 2) Execute traffic-slice reduction to 5% for affected variants. 3) Trigger automated fallback to previous model variant for 20% of affected traffic. 4) Notify product, SRE, and legal via the rollout channel with prefilled template (see comms templates).\n- For OSCILLATION detection: 1) Pin routing to last-stable variant, disable reactive routing for 15m, increase synthetic probe cadence. 2) Do not rollback immediately; allow 15m for stabilization unless other signals (eval drop or cost spike) co-occur.\n- For COST_SPIKE: 1) Throttle nonessential background workloads; 2) Notify finance and solutions-eng; 3) If cost multiplier > 3x for 30m escalate to billing committee with suggested temporary cap.
communication_templates: - Slack snippet (automated): '[Rollout-Sim] ALERT: StabilityScore=58 for feature XYZ at 2026-02-28T14:12Z. Auto-fallback executed for 20% traffic. P99=1420ms (SLO=500ms). See RG-2187 for timeline.'\n- Pager template: 'Pager: Feature XYZ (rollout id: R-2026-02-28-xyz). Condition: Behavior drift detected (eval drop 6%). Action recommended: pause exposure and run human review. Contact: @product-steward, @sre-oncall.'\n- Stakeholder email (short): Subject: 'Staged rollout: pause + rollback recommendation for XYZ' Body: one-paragraph summary, impact numbers, next steps, and link to incident timeline.
checklist_for_canary_wave: - Pre-wave: verify synthetic probes green x3 windows, autopilot quotas set, cost safety cap enabled. - During wave: watch StabilityScore dashboard, confirm no user-facing error reports, ensure human-review panel on-call. - Post-wave: run 24h focused eval sweep, commit to postmortem if any contingency state was entered.
metrics_to_record_in_postsim: - Time to detection (first signal to alert). - Time to mitigation (alert to action: auto-fallback or traffic reduction). - False positive rate (simulated condition triggered mitigation but cause benign). - Operator steps and manual interventions count. - Residual user-facing error delta after mitigation.
open_questions: What should be the exact weighting for StabilityScore in enterprise accounts with higher cost sensitivity?
How long should reactive routing be disabled in persistent thrash scenarios (15m vs 30m)?
Do we prefer auto-rollback to previous model or auto-fallback to quantized variant for cost spikes?
Which organization owns the 'billing committee' temporary cap approval?
next_steps: - Run the Scenario A/B suite with the new StabilityScore thresholds and capture timelines (owner: Samir, target cycle: 2026-03-10). - Draft a short training play for oncall engineers to run the simulator locally (owner: Theo). - Add two more synthetic probes targeting multilingual corner cases (owner: Lena). - Validate comms templates with the comms guild and legal (owner: Elena).
notes_to_self: Keep iterations small — prefer 3 compact simulation scenarios that cross teams rather than a huge matrix. Focus on observability gaps first; you can't decide on thresholds you can't measure. Save the large-scale blackout simulations for a separate SRE disaster-recovery exercise.
